tc.research_page.GT_INFUSION_INTERCEPTER:
Between the moments of an Infusion ritual, you discovered an apparatus that does not belong to any conventional school of Arcane study — the Infusion Interceptor. It does not cast spells. Instead, it intercepts the ritual itself, binding the flow of arcane power that once required a wizard's constant attention within a cold and silent vessel.
Place it 3 to 10 blocks beneath the Runic Matrix, and the Interceptor will recognize the Matrix and its pedestals on its own. It will search the 13×13×3 space below for containers of Essentia, drawing forth whatever is required as quietly as though the Matrix had never asked anyone for it.
Once the offering is placed upon the central pedestal, the ritual will begin by itself. No wand. No incantation. No need to touch those dangerous runes ever again.

More unsettling still, the Interceptor appears capable of taking upon itself a portion of the 'uncertainty' inherent to an Infusion ritual. Recipes that would once have given even seasoned thaumaturges pause become strangely quiet in its presence.
Once all required Essentia has been gathered, the Interceptor will claim every offering upon the pedestals at once, completing the Infusion in a single instant. There is no lengthy incantation, no gradual build-up of the ritual, and no discernible moment between beginning and completion.
Some believe that what lies within the Interceptor is not merely arcane data, but a kind of 'memory of the ritual' itself. Thus, even when its master has departed this world, it continues its work — like a tireless scribe, completing unfinished rites in the hours when no one is watching.
During your studies of the Arcane Bath, you caught a glimpse of a truth that was never meant to be seen. From that revelation came a peculiar elixir known as Pure Tears — a liquid said to be untouched even by the Warp itself.
Drink it, and every distortion clinging to your being will fade as though it had never existed. Permanent Warp, temporary Warp, even the tenacious stains that cling like an obsession—all shall be washed away.
The ancient formula demanded a price from those who dared to drink it. The modern recipe has removed that price from the cup. All that remains is the draught, and the quiet moment in which your soul remembers how to be still.
Yet purity should not be accepted lightly. There are secrets that reveal themselves only to the distorted, and when the Warp is gone, something besides madness may vanish with it.
